display.title: Episode 19: Life in the Hand of the Tongue, Chapter 1 (Pesach)
display.summary_short: A Chol HaMoed Pesach show on guarding our words: why speech is like an arrow, and the start of the story of a hunter, a lion's milk and a quarrel among the parts of the body.
display.summary_long: A Chol HaMoed Pesach 5742 program. Uncle Yossi wishes everyone a kosher and happy Pesach, explains that Hashem's blessings come in full measure when we are b'simcha, especially on Yom Tov, and leads a victory march, played on Pesach pots and spoons instead of the chametz-dik drumsticks. He introduces the Chofetz Chaim and his emphasis on shemiras halashon, and teaches that words are like an arrow: once released they cannot be called back, which is why Hashem guarded the tongue with 32 teeth and two lips. A young girl leads the Shema in Studio 604. Then the story begins: a kind king falls gravely ill and can be cured only with lion's milk. A brave hunter uses ten goats to befriend a lion and fills a bucket with its milk. On his way back he dreams that his feet, hands, brain, eyes and ears each claim the reward, and they all laugh at the tongue, which vows to prove it is king of the body. The show ends with letters from a boy who listens on his school bus and a girl's Purim poem about the gragger.
display.lesson: Words are like arrows: once they leave your mouth you cannot take them back, so think before you speak.

date.note: 'In the midst of... Pesach'; episode 18 announced this show for Tuesday morning at the end of Chol HaMoed.
